rules.statement: When a new order is started it is pre-filled: the salesperson is the signed-in employee, the tax rate is the default sales tax rate from system settings, the status is New and the order date is the current date and time. The default tax rate is stored in system settings as a whole number of thousandths and divided by 1000 when read.
Choosing the customer of an order sets the order's tax status to that customer's standard tax status; the user may still change it while the order is New.
The customer of an order is chosen only from companies whose type is Customer, and the shipper only from companies whose type is Shipper; both choice lists are sorted by company name.
Order lines cannot be entered until the order itself has been saved; trying to do so shows a message and sends the user back to the customer field.

A record on the order, order line, company, contact or employee screens cannot be saved while any column that the table marks as required is blank; the save is refused with a message and the blank required fields are highlighted until the record is saved.
An order line's quantity must be greater than zero.
A product can appear at most once on the same order (one line per order and product).

On an order line the product list can be narrowed to one product category (or show all products); choosing a product copies the product's current list price into the line's unit price, and the line's discount starts at zero. A line whose chosen product has no price gets no product.

A new order line starts with status New. When the line is saved with both a product and a quantity, its status becomes Allocated if the product's available stock (computed by the inventory area) covers the whole quantity, otherwise No Stock.

After an order line is saved, changed to another product, or deleted, stock allocation is run again for the affected product (and for the previous product when the product was changed), so waiting lines of other orders can move between Allocated, On Order and No Stock, oldest order first. Deleting a line asks for confirmation first.
Deleting an order asks for confirmation, deletes all its lines with it and re-runs stock allocation for each of those lines' products.
An order can be deleted only while its status is New or Invoiced; deleting a Shipped, Paid or Closed order is refused with a message, and deleting an unsaved order does nothing.
Order lines can be added, changed or deleted only while the order is unsaved or New; once the order is invoiced its lines are read-only.

Which order fields can be edited depends on the order status: on an unsaved order the customer, salesperson, notes, shipping fee, tax rate and tax status; when New the notes, shipping fee, tax rate and tax status (customer and salesperson are fixed once saved); when Invoiced the notes, shipped date and shipper; when Shipped the notes, payment method and paid date; when Paid only the notes; when Closed nothing. Order number, status, order date, invoice date, tax amount and total are never edited by hand. No order is enforced between the order, invoice, shipped and paid dates; the new app adds no date checks.

Creating the invoice is allowed only for a New order that has at least one line, all of whose lines are Allocated (no partial invoices), and whose shipping fee is filled in (zero is accepted, blank is not; the blank field is highlighted). It saves the order, opens the invoice, sets the status to Invoiced, stamps the invoice date with the current date and time and sets every line to Invoiced. Partial invoices and backorders stay unsupported.

Shipping is allowed only for an Invoiced order and needs the shipped date, the shipper and the shipping fee (missing ones are highlighted and the user is told); it sets the order to Shipped and every line to Shipped. The shipped date may be any date; no check against the order or invoice date.

Receiving payment is allowed only for a Shipped order and needs the payment method (one of the fixed methods offered by the order screen) and the paid date (missing ones are highlighted and the user is told); it sets the order to Paid. The paid date may be any date; no check against the order or shipped date.
Closing is allowed only for a Paid order and only after the user confirms; it sets the order to Closed, after which nothing on the order can be edited.
Once an order is past New, its invoice can be opened again at any time; reopening it never changes the order or its lines. On an unsaved or New order the reprint action is not offered.

The invoice is a printable document for one order: the invoice number is the order number; it shows the date it is printed (not the stored invoice date, so a reprint carries the new date), the customer's name and address (as bill-to and ship-to), the salesperson's full name and the trading company's own address (the company whose type is the trading company itself); one row per line with product code, product name, quantity, unit price, discount and extended price = quantity x unit price x (1 - discount); then subtotal = sum of extended prices, tax = tax rate x subtotal when the order's tax status is Taxable and 0 otherwise (shipping is not taxed), shipping = the order's shipping fee, and total = subtotal + tax + shipping.
Opening the invoice for an order that has no lines shows a 'nothing to print' message instead of an empty invoice.

The order screen shows each line's price = quantity x (1 - discount) x unit price, the lines' subtotal, the tax amount = tax rate x subtotal when the order's tax status is Taxable and 0 otherwise, and the order total = subtotal + tax amount + shipping fee (a blank fee counts as 0). A shipping fee of zero is accepted and is never taxed.
An order's total is the sum over its lines of quantity x (1 - discount) x unit price, without tax and shipping; an order without lines has no total (blank).

The order list shows every order whose customer is a Customer-type company, newest order number first, with the customer name, the salesperson's full name, the order total, the order status name, the order date without its time, and the least advanced status among its lines (the line status with the lowest sort order; blank when the order has no lines).

The order list has four filters: Open orders (every status except Closed), Recent orders (order date within the last 30 days; when there are none the user is told), My orders (salesperson is the signed-in employee) and All orders. Any filter left over from an earlier session is cleared when the list opens and the selected filter is applied. The list opens with the Open orders filter selected.
The order list footer shows the number of orders and the sum of their order totals for the rows currently shown.

The employee screen's recent orders list takes the 20 most recent orders of all employees (newest order number first), then shows only those that belong to the selected employee, with date, total, status, salesperson and customer; an employee with no order among those 20 sees an empty list.

For a Customer company the company screen lists all its orders (newest first) with salesperson, shipper, total and status; for a Shipper company it lists the orders it shipped with salesperson, customer, total and status; for a Vendor it shows its purchase orders (purchasing area); for the trading company itself it shows no orders.

Orders are opened from the order list, from a company's order lists and from an employee's recent orders, and a new order is started from the order list; each opens the order screen for that order (or a blank new order), several orders can be open side by side, and when an order screen closes the open list screens are refreshed. Double-clicking a line's product opens that product's screen.

An order moves only forward through New, Invoiced, Shipped, Paid and Closed, one step at a time and only through its actions (create invoice, ship, receive payment, close); the next available action is highlighted on the order screen and actions offered out of turn are refused with a message.

Every table with audit columns records who created a row and when, and who last changed it and when: inserting sets created-by, created-on, modified-by and modified-on; updating sets modified-by and modified-on and keeps the original created-by and created-on even if an update tries to change or blank them. The name recorded is the signed-in employee's full name (first then last); there is no fallback to the operating-system login. Rows written by imports, start-up jobs and other system jobs, where nobody is signed in, carry the fixed name System.
The order, company and employee screens show a one-line history of the record: when and by whom it was created and when and by whom it was last modified, leaving out the parts that are blank.

A company cannot be deleted while it has orders as customer, orders as shipper or purchase orders as vendor; the user is told how many of each. Otherwise the user confirms (the message says how many contacts and vendor-product links will go too) and the company is deleted together with its contacts and its vendor-product links. The cascade to contacts and vendor-product links is kept.
A company's type cannot be changed while it has orders as customer, orders as shipper, purchase orders as vendor or vendor-product links; the change is undone and the user is told why.
The company screen is titled with the company type and shows the related list that fits the type (customer orders, shipped orders, or purchase orders), switching as soon as the type changes.
Saving changes on the company screen asks the user to confirm; answering no discards the unsaved changes. The other screens keep saving without asking.

The company list is read-only and can be filtered to Customers, Shippers, Vendors or all companies (the heading follows the filter). Opening a company or adding one from the list opens the company screen restricted to the same filter, with a new company defaulting to the filtered type; only one company screen can be open at a time.
Typing a customer name that does not exist yet in the order's customer field opens the company screen on a new company with that name filled in.

Company lists show companies sorted by name with a one-line business address built from street, city, state and zip, plus the company type and standard tax status names; contacts are sorted by last then first name.

An employee cannot be deleted while they have orders, have submitted purchase orders, supervise other employees or hold privileges; the user is told every reason. Otherwise the user confirms the delete by the employee's name.
An employee cannot be their own supervisor: the supervisor list leaves out the employee being edited. Typing a supervisor who is not an employee offers to start a new employee record.
After a new employee is saved, the privilege assignment screen opens for that employee so privileges can be granted straight away.
An employee's full name is shown as first name then last name in choice lists (sorted that way) and as last name, first name for the employee list (sorted that way).

An employee's courtesy title must be one of the titles in the titles list; a title that is not in the list can be added from the employee screen through a small title-entry screen pre-filled with the typed value.

Phone numbers of companies, contacts and employees are entered as a ten-digit number shown as 3-3-4 digits, optionally followed by an extension of up to eight characters. Only this US format is accepted; international numbers are not.

Names are unique: a company name once per company type, a contact's first and last name once per company, an employee's first and last name once (a duplicate is refused with a message), an operating-system login on at most one employee, and status, type, tax status, privilege and title names once each.

Order statuses, order line statuses, tax statuses and company types are fixed code lists that the logic depends on by identity (order: New, Invoiced, Shipped, Paid, Closed; line: New, Allocated, No Stock, On Order, Invoiced, Shipped; tax: Tax Exempt, Taxable; company: Customer, Shipper, Vendor and the trading company itself). Status choice lists are sorted by their sort order, company types by name, tax statuses by code and states by state name.
A new company's standard tax status defaults to Tax Exempt until the user picks another. Customers also default to Tax Exempt.

At start-up (the auto-run macro, when the database is trusted) the start-up routine runs: on the very first run only, guarded by the first-run flag in system settings, it moves every date in every table forward by the number of days between the latest order date and today (never backwards) so the sample data looks current, then sets the flag so this never runs again; it then shows the welcome screen when that setting is on, asks the user to sign in and opens the order list. The new app keeps the date shift as a one-off start-up command guarded by the same first-run flag; rows it changes are stamped with the name System (R-orders-031).
After the user signs in, the order list is the first screen shown.

A product's physical stock (available quantity) is the quantity counted at its most recent stock take, plus every purchase-order line quantity for the product received at or after that stock take's date and time, minus every order line quantity for the product whose order was invoiced at or after that moment. Orders with no invoice date are not counted as sold, and purchase-order lines with no received date are not counted as bought. Stock therefore leaves the warehouse, for these figures, at the invoice date, for every line of an invoiced order whatever the line's own status; the client confirmed this point.

The stock take that counts for a product is the one with the latest date and time. Every product has an opening stock take of quantity zero, so its stock figures always have a starting point. The new app creates it when the product is created, dated at the product's creation date and time. A product that still has none (for example one loaded from the old data) gets it the first time its stock is calculated, dated at the product's added date, or now when that is unknown, as the original does. Either way every stock figure is the same as in the original.

A product's allocated quantity is the total quantity of its order lines in the Allocated line status, and its no-stock quantity is the total quantity of its order lines in the No Stock line status; a product with no such lines has zero.

A product's on-order quantity is the total quantity of the product on purchase-order lines whose purchase order is in the Approved status. Purchase orders that are New, Submitted, Received or Closed do not count. New and Submitted purchase orders stay out of the on-order figure on purpose, although the reorder action treats them as outstanding (R-inventory-017).
A product's quantity to sell is its physical stock (R-inventory-001) minus its allocated quantity (R-inventory-003). It can be negative.

The suggested reorder quantity compares supply (quantity to sell plus on-order quantity) with demand (no-stock quantity plus the product's target level, a blank target counting as zero). When supply covers demand the suggestion is the product's minimum reorder quantity (1 when blank). Otherwise it is the shortfall (demand minus supply), raised to the minimum reorder quantity when the shortfall is smaller. Only Approved purchase orders count as on order here (R-inventory-004).

Allocating stock to orders for a product goes through its order lines in the Allocated, No Stock or On Order line status, oldest order date first (lower order number first on a tie). A line becomes Allocated only if its whole quantity fits in the physical stock still unallocated; otherwise it becomes On Order if its whole quantity fits in the remaining physical stock plus the on-order quantity; otherwise it becomes No Stock. Lines are never part-allocated, and a later smaller line can be allocated when an earlier larger one could not.
Saving a stock take re-runs the stock allocation (R-inventory-007) for that product, so order line statuses follow the new count straight away.

A stock take records the counted quantity on hand for a product. Its date and time are set by the system to the moment it is saved; the user cannot enter them, so a count cannot be back-dated. The expected quantity stored with it is the product's physical stock (R-inventory-001) calculated at that moment. The counted and expected quantities can never be negative, and date, product and counted quantity are required.

When the counted quantity entered for a stock take differs from the expected quantity, the user is shown both figures and must confirm the count; if they decline, the entry is discarded and nothing is saved.
Stock takes are append-only: users may add a new stock take for a product, but an existing stock take can be neither edited nor deleted.

A product cannot be saved while any required field is empty (code, name, standard unit cost, unit price, category, discontinued flag) or while its standard unit cost is zero or less. Product code and product name are each unique.

A product's code is built from a fixed company prefix (NWT), the code of the product's category, a hyphen and the product's number. It is set whenever a category is chosen for a product that already has a number, so changing a product's category changes its code. The prefix and the rebuild on a category change are kept as they are; codes are not frozen once issued.
A product category's code cannot be changed once any product belongs to that category, because product codes are built from it. Category name and category code are each required and unique.
A product category cannot be deleted while any product belongs to it; the user is told why. An unsaved new category is simply discarded.

A product cannot be deleted while it appears on any order line or any purchase-order line; the user is told which kind of record blocks it and nothing is deleted. Otherwise the user is asked to confirm the delete. On confirmation the product, its stock takes and its vendor links are deleted together in one step; if the user declines, nothing is deleted. (The original removed the stock takes and vendor links before asking, so declining left the product without them; the new app does not reproduce that partial delete.)

Reordering a product first saves any pending changes to it. If the product has an on-order quantity and there is a purchase order in the Approved, New or Submitted status that contains the product, reordering opens that purchase order instead of creating or changing anything. New and Submitted purchase orders count as outstanding here, although they do not count in the on-order figure (R-inventory-004).

A product can be reordered only when at least one vendor is linked to it; otherwise the user is told a vendor is required and sent to the product's vendors. With exactly one linked vendor that vendor is used; with several the user picks one, and cancelling the choice cancels the reorder.

The reorder quantity is the suggested reorder quantity (R-inventory-006). If that is zero, the product's minimum reorder quantity is used; if that is also zero or blank, the user is asked for a quantity, and a zero or cancelled answer cancels the reorder.

A reorder adds the product to the chosen vendor's oldest purchase order still in the New status: if the product is already on that order its line quantity is increased, otherwise a line is added. When the vendor has no New purchase order, a new purchase order in the New status is created for the vendor with that single line. The line's unit cost is the product's standard unit cost. If no purchase order results, the user is told the reorder failed. If the line cannot be added to that purchase order, the user is told that the purchase order exists without it.

A discontinued product cannot be reordered (the reorder action is not offered) and its discontinued status is shown prominently. The reorder quantity is highlighted as needing attention only for a product that is not discontinued and whose suggested reorder quantity is above zero.

The product page shows, for a saved product, its quantity to sell, no-stock, allocated and on-order quantities and its suggested reorder quantity, recalculated whenever the product or its target level changes. A product that is not yet saved shows zeros and offers no delete, reorder, order history or purchase-order history.

The product list shows every product with its category name, code, name, description, costs and prices, reorder settings and discontinued flag, together with its calculated no-stock, allocated, to-sell and on-order quantities.

From the product list a user can download an .xlsx spreadsheet listing, per product sorted by name, its number, code and name, allocated quantity, quantity to sell, on-order quantity, reorder level, target level, minimum reorder quantity and discontinued flag. The download from the web page replaces the Access spreadsheet export.

A product's order history lists each order line for the product with the order number and date, quantity, unit price, extended price (quantity times unit price), the order's status name and the line's status name.

A product's purchase-order history lists each purchase-order line for the product with the purchase order number, status, quantity, unit cost, extended cost (quantity times unit cost), vendor name, submitted date and received date, ordered by the status's sort order and then the submitted date.

When picking a product on an order line, the category filter offers an 'all categories' entry first and then every category by name; the product choices, sorted by name with their unit price and category, are all products when 'all' is chosen and only that category's products otherwise. Discontinued products are included and stay selectable on order lines.

Products, product categories, product-vendor links and stock takes carry audit stamps. When a record is created, the added-by and modified-by fields get the signed-in user's full name (first name then last name) and the added-on and modified-on fields the current date and time; on every later change only the modified-by and modified-on fields are refreshed, and the added-by and added-on values can never be changed or cleared. Only the signed-in user is recorded; there is no fallback to an operating-system login. Records written with no signed-in user, by imports, start-up jobs and other system jobs, carry the fixed name System.
A product can be linked to a given vendor only once; product and vendor are both required on the link, and the vendor must be an existing company.

End to end, a user can open the product list, open a product whose stock is short of its target, see its levels and suggested reorder quantity, reorder it from a linked vendor, and find the resulting New purchase order on the product's purchase-order history; once that order is approved the quantity shows as on order, and once it is received the product's physical stock rises and waiting order lines are allocated.
A new purchase order always starts in status New, whether it is entered by hand or created by a product reorder.

A purchase order is saved only when its required fields are filled in (at least the vendor and the status); otherwise the save is refused and the missing fields are highlighted. The vendor must be an existing company, the status an existing purchase order status, and the submitter and approver existing employees.

A purchase order moves through the fixed sequence New, Submitted, Approved, Received, Closed. Each step has its own action, each action works only from the status directly before it, and no step can be skipped or undone. The form shows which steps are already done.

Submitting is allowed only for a purchase order in status New. It records the signed-in user as submitter and the current date and time (date and time, not the date alone) as the submitted date, and sets the status to Submitted. From any other status the action is refused with a message and nothing changes.

Approving is allowed only for a Submitted purchase order and only for a user who holds the approve-purchase-order privilege. The approver may be the same person who submitted it (self-approval is allowed). Approving records that user as approver and the current date and time as the approved date, and sets the status to Approved. Without the privilege, or from another status, the action is refused with a message and nothing changes.

Right after a purchase order is approved, and again right after it is received, stock allocation is re-run for every product on it, so customer order lines waiting for those products are re-evaluated oldest first (the allocation rule itself belongs to the inventory area).

Receiving is allowed only for an Approved purchase order and only after the user confirms posting it to inventory; declining changes nothing. Receiving records the current date and time as the received date of the purchase order and of every one of its lines (the whole order is received at once; there are no partial receipts of some lines or part quantities) and sets the status to Received.

Stock update: once a line is received, its quantity counts as stock bought from its received date and time, so it raises the product's available quantity after the last stock take. While its purchase order is Approved and not yet received, the line quantity counts as on order instead.

Closing is allowed only for a Received purchase order and only when both the shipping fee and the payment method are filled in; otherwise the missing fields are highlighted and the close is refused. Closing stores the current date and time as the payment date, the computed tax as the tax amount and the computed total as the payment amount, and sets the status to Closed. The payment method is chosen from a fixed list of exactly three methods: credit card, check and cash.

Purchase order amounts: each line amount is quantity times unit cost; the subtotal is the sum of the line amounts; the tax is the vendor tax rate times the subtotal, where the vendor tax rate is one system-wide setting (the shipping fee is not taxed, and the tax is stored on the purchase order only when it is closed); the total is subtotal plus tax plus shipping fee, with a missing shipping fee counted as zero.

Field locking by status: once a purchase order is saved, its number, vendor, status, submitter, approver, the submitted and approved dates, the computed tax and total and the payment date can no longer be edited directly. The received date is editable only while the order is Approved, the shipping fee and payment method only while it is Received, and the notes until it is Closed. A Closed purchase order is read-only. On a new, unsaved purchase order the vendor can be chosen; once the purchase order is saved its vendor is fixed in every status.
Line items can be added, changed or deleted only while the purchase order is New (or not yet saved); from Submitted on the lines are frozen.
Line items cannot be entered before the purchase order itself has been saved; the user is told to complete and save the purchase order first.
A purchase order can be deleted only while it is New or Submitted; deleting it also deletes all of its lines. In any later status the delete is refused with a message.

The vendor of a purchase order is chosen before the purchase order is first saved, without any confirmation, and choosing it refreshes the product choices for the lines. Once the purchase order is saved its vendor can never be changed, in any status; there is no change-vendor action, so the original's confirm-and-delete-all-lines prompt (reachable only on a saved purchase order, where the vendor is already locked) is not carried over.

The product choices for a purchase order line are only the products that the purchase order's vendor supplies (per the product-vendor list), sorted by product name, each carrying its standard unit cost.
The vendor choices for a purchase order are the companies whose company type is vendor, sorted by company name.

Choosing a product on a purchase order line fills in the quantity with the product's computed reorder quantity and the unit cost with the product's standard unit cost; the user may change both before saving.

A purchase order line needs a product, a quantity and a unit cost, and the product must exist. A quantity below the product's minimum reorder quantity is refused with a message. If the product's quantity available to sell plus the ordered quantity stays below the product's target level, the user gets a warning only and the line is still saved (it is never a hard stop).

A purchase order holds at most one line per product. Adding a product that is already on the purchase order adds the new quantity to the existing line and keeps its unit cost; the database also refuses a second line for the same product.

On a saved purchase order, one action adds a line for every product that the vendor supplies, that is not yet on the purchase order and that has at least one customer order line waiting in No Stock status; each new line gets the product's computed reorder quantity and its standard unit cost. On an unsaved purchase order the action is refused with a message.

When a product with several vendors is reordered, the user picks the vendor from a dialog that lists only the vendors supplying that product, sorted by name. Confirming without a vendor selected is refused with a prompt, a double-click on a vendor confirms it, and cancel ends the reorder without creating anything. A product with exactly one vendor skips the dialog, and a product without a vendor cannot be reordered.
The extended cost of a purchase order is the sum over its lines of quantity times unit cost; a purchase order without lines still appears, with no cost.

The purchase order list shows every purchase order with its status, vendor name, submitter and approver names, submitted, approved and payment dates, and a total cost equal to extended cost plus shipping fee plus tax amount (missing parts count as zero), ordered by purchase order number with the newest first. The list footer shows the number of purchase orders and the sum of their total cost.

On a vendor's company page, the purchase order tab lists that vendor's purchase orders with status, submitter, approver, the submitted, approved and received dates, the payment fields and the extended cost, plus a count; only purchase orders that have a submitter appear, so New purchase orders are not listed there (kept on purpose). Double-clicking a row opens that purchase order.

Audit fields on purchase orders, purchase order lines and purchase order statuses: on insert, added-by, added-on, modified-by and modified-on are set to the stamp name and the current date and time; on every update, modified-by and modified-on are refreshed while added-by and added-on keep their original values even if an edit tries to change or clear them. The stamp name is the signed-in user's full name (first name then last name); there is no operating-system login fallback. Rows written without a signed-in user (imports, start-up jobs and other system jobs) carry the fixed name System. The purchase order form shows who created and last changed the record.
When the report selection page opens, the monthly sales per employee report is already selected and its date range inputs are shown, exactly as if the user had chosen that report.

Choosing one of the three sales reports (monthly per employee, monthly per product, quarterly per product) shows a start date and an end date input. The end date defaults to the calendar date of the most recent order date in the database and the start date to the same day three calendar months earlier. Choosing the product catalog hides both inputs and clears them. The page always shows the name of the report currently chosen.

The sales report queries take their period from the start and end dates entered on the report selection page. When a sales report is run without that page (for example from a link or a scheduled export), the period defaults to the same range: from three calendar months before the date of the latest order up to that date.

Monthly sales per employee: for each salesperson and each calendar month, the report value is the sum of the order totals of that salesperson's orders whose order date falls between the start and end dates (inclusive bounds, compared against the full order date and time). An order total is the sum over its lines of quantity times unit price times one minus the line discount; an order without lines adds nothing. Orders of every status are counted. Months are labelled by abbreviated month name and year and sorted by year then month.

Monthly sales per product: for each product and each calendar month, the value is the sum over order lines of quantity times unit price times one minus the line discount, for orders whose order date falls between the start and end dates. Orders of every status are counted. Months are labelled by abbreviated month name and year and sorted by year then month.

Quarterly sales per product: the same net line amounts as the monthly product report, grouped by product and calendar quarter of the order date within the start and end dates. Each quarter is labelled by its quarter number followed by the year.
Each sales report prints the order-date range it covers in its header, using the start and end dates chosen on the report selection page.
When a sales report has no orders in the chosen period, the user is told that the report has no data and the report is not opened.

The monthly sales per employee report opens in an interactive view. It offers a list of the salespeople that appear in the report plus an entry for all employees; picking a salesperson limits the rows, totals and chart to that person, and picking the all-employees entry removes the limit.

The monthly and quarterly sales per product reports list each product's sales within each period, show a subtotal for every month or quarter and a grand total for the whole range, and include a chart of sales by product. Every sales report shows the time it was produced and page numbers in the form page n of m. The quarterly report lists its quarters in order of year, then quarter number, instead of the original's order of the quarter-first label, which mixed years; its chart shows the monthly figures of the period, as in the original (Q-reports-004).

Lifetime sales per product is the sum over all of the product's order lines of quantity times unit price times one minus the line discount, with no date or status filter. The catalog lists every product that belongs to a product category, with its category, name, id, quantity per unit, unit price and lifetime sales; a product that was never sold is still listed, with no sales.

In the product catalog each category section shows the category description and image, the number of priced items, the lowest and the highest unit price, and the total lifetime sales of its products, followed by the product list. The image shown for each category is the image stored with that category, as in the original; the original's switched-off code that loaded category images from files is not carried over (Q-reports-006).

The product catalog has a table of contents that lists each product category once with the page on which its section starts. To get correct page numbers the catalog is rendered in full to PDF first, recording each category's starting page; the catalog is then shown with that table of contents. The previous table of contents is discarded at the start of every full generation. If no table of contents has been generated yet, the catalog shows a note telling the user to generate the PDF. The catalog is generated on demand and not stored; there is one edition (Q-reports-005).

The product catalog also contains fixed pages: a quality statement and a gastronomic introduction whose texts come from the application's maintained text strings, and an order form that shows the selling company's own address and business phone (the company whose company type marks it as the house company) with a tick-box list of the shippers a customer can choose.
When the product catalog has no rows, the user is told that the report has no data, but the catalog still opens.

The main menu has a Reports entry that opens the report selection page. The Preview action opens the chosen report: the monthly sales per employee report in its interactive view, the product catalog and the product sales reports as a print preview that can be saved as PDF.

workflows.title: Order entry to invoice (printable PDF) to shipping
steps: sign in and land on the order list
start a new order and choose the customer
save the order header
add order lines (each line is allocated or marked no stock)
create the invoice and download it as a PDF
enter shipped date, shipper and shipping fee and ship the order
enter payment method and paid date and receive payment
close the order

workflows.title: Inventory levels and restocking
steps: open a product's stock takes and enter a counted quantity
when the count differs from the expected quantity, confirm it
see the stock take saved with the system date and the expected quantity, and the product's figures and order line allocations updated
open the product list and read each product's stock figures
open a product whose quantity to sell is below its target level and check its suggested reorder quantity
reorder it, picking the vendor in the dialog when the product has several vendors
see the product added to the vendor's oldest New purchase order, or a new one, on the product's purchase-order history
after that purchase order is approved and received, see the physical stock rise and waiting order lines allocated

workflows.title: Purchase order to receiving to stock update
steps: open the purchase order list and start a new purchase order
choose the vendor and save the purchase order (status New)
add line items for the vendor's products, or add all no-stock products at once
submit the purchase order
approve it as a user with the approve-purchase-order privilege (its quantities now count as on order)
receive it after confirming (status Received; the received quantities raise available stock)
check the product's available stock on the product page
enter the shipping fee and payment method and close it (tax, payment amount and payment date stored)

workflows.title: The invoice and the four chosen reports
steps: open an invoiced order and open its invoice again as a PDF
open Reports from the main menu and see monthly sales per employee preselected with the default period
change the start and end dates, preview the report and filter it to one salesperson
switch to monthly and to quarterly sales per product and preview each
save a sales report as PDF
choose the product catalog, see the date inputs hidden, and generate it
check the table of contents, the fixed pages and the order form with the shipper list
save the catalog as PDF

open_questions.text: The printed invoice shows the date it is printed, not the stored invoice date, so a reprint carries a new date. Should the invoice show the stored invoice date instead? (Assumption until answered: keep the original behaviour.) Answer (2026-10-16, demo client): keep the original: the invoice shows the date it is printed.

The original enforces no rules on the invoice, shipped and paid dates (they can be any date, also before the order date). Should the new app require shipped date and paid date to be on or after the order date (and paid on or after shipped)? (Assumption: no extra date checks.) Answer (2026-10-16, demo client): no extra date checks.

Tax is charged on the line subtotal only, never on the shipping fee, and a shipping fee of zero is accepted while a blank fee blocks invoicing. Is that correct for your business? (Assumption: keep as is.) Answer (2026-10-16, demo client): keep as is: tax on the line subtotal only, zero fee accepted, blank fee blocks invoicing.

The employee screen's recent orders list is built from the 20 most recent orders overall and then narrowed to the employee, so an employee may see fewer than 20 or none. Should it show the employee's own 20 most recent orders instead? (Assumption: keep the current behaviour, as R-orders-027 states and its equivalence unit proves. If you choose the employee's own 20 most recent before sign-off, R-orders-027 is restated and proven by a rule test instead; after sign-off it is a change order.) Answer (2026-10-16, demo client): keep the current behaviour (R-orders-027, proven by its equivalence unit).

On the first start the original shifts every date in the database forward so the sample data looks current. Keep this as a one-off start-up command in the new app (useful for demo data), or drop it? (Assumption: keep as a one-off command guarded by the first-run flag.) Answer (2026-10-16, demo client): keep as a one-off start-up command guarded by the first-run flag.

Saving a company asks 'do you want to save your changes?' while other screens save without asking. Keep the confirmation for companies? (Assumption: keep.) Answer (2026-10-16, demo client): keep the confirmation for companies.

Deleting a company that has no orders or purchase orders also deletes its contacts and vendor-product links after one confirmation. Is that cascade wanted? (Assumption: yes.) Answer (2026-10-16, demo client): yes, keep the cascade.

These Access conveniences are dropped and replaced by standard web features: the recently-used list on the ribbon, export of any list to Excel, the mailing-label wizard, the 'click to map' link, e-mailing the company screen, the show-filter and show/hide-columns buttons. Is any of them needed in the new app? Answer (2026-10-16, demo client): none is needed; the xlsx export of lists (admin export), browser bookmarks and the list filters replace them; no mailing labels, map link or e-mailing of the company screen.
Which order list filter should be selected when the list opens? The design does not record the default. (Assumption: Open orders.) Answer (2026-10-16, demo client): Open orders.

Phone numbers are forced into a US ten-digit format with an optional extension. Keep the US format, or accept international numbers? (Assumption: keep the US format.) Answer (2026-10-16, demo client): keep the US format.
A new company is tax exempt by default. Should new customers default to Taxable instead? (Assumption: keep exempt.) Answer (2026-10-16, demo client): keep Tax Exempt as the default.

An order can be invoiced only when every line is Allocated (no partial invoices or backorders). Is that still the rule? (Assumption: yes.) Answer (2026-10-16, demo client): yes, every line must be Allocated.

Only Approved purchase orders count as on order in the stock figures and the suggested reorder quantity, while the reorder action also treats New and Submitted orders as outstanding. Should New and Submitted orders keep being left out of the on-order figure?

When a product has no stock take, the old app silently creates an opening zero-quantity stock take the first time stock is calculated. May the new app create that opening stock take when the product is created instead (same figures)?
Stock takes are always dated at the moment they are saved, so a count made earlier cannot be back-dated. Keep that restriction?
Is the spreadsheet export of the product list still needed, and is an .xlsx download from the web page acceptable?
Discontinued products are still offered when picking a product on an order line. Should they stay selectable for new orders?

Audit stamps record the signed-in employee's full name; the old app falls back to the Windows user name when nobody is signed in. The web app always has a signed-in user, so we record that user only. Is that acceptable for every table with audit fields, and which name should stamps from imports or system jobs carry?

Product codes are rebuilt from the fixed NWT prefix, the category code and the product number whenever the category changes. Keep the prefix and the rebuild on category change, or should codes stay fixed once issued?
Sold quantity counts every line of an invoiced order from the invoice date on, whatever the line's own status. Is that the intended point at which stock leaves the warehouse (rather than shipping)?

Once a purchase order is saved its vendor is locked in every status, yet the app also has a confirm-and-delete-all-lines path for changing the vendor. Should the vendor of a saved New purchase order be changeable (deleting its lines after confirmation), or fixed once the purchase order is saved, as the current app effectively behaves?

The purchase order tab on a vendor's company page lists only purchase orders that already have a submitter, so New purchase orders do not appear there, while the main purchase order list shows them. Is that intended, or should the vendor tab show every purchase order of the vendor?

Tax on a purchase order is the vendor tax rate from the system settings times the line subtotal, the shipping fee is not taxed, and the tax is stored only when the purchase order is closed. Please confirm, and confirm that the vendor tax rate stays a single system-wide setting.
Any user with the approve-purchase-order privilege can approve, including the person who submitted the purchase order. Should self-approval be blocked?
Receiving is all or nothing: the whole purchase order is received at once and every line gets the same received date. Do you need partial receipts (some lines or part quantities)?

The table design describes the submitted, approved, received and payment dates as dates without a time, but the app stores the date and time. Should the new app keep date and time (the line received time matters for stock calculations) or store dates only on the purchase order?

The received date stays editable while a purchase order is Approved, and the shipping fee and payment method only while it is Received. Is that intended? Also, the payment method is chosen from a fixed list of three (credit card, check, cash): is that the full list?
When a line's quantity leaves the product below its target level, the app only warns and still saves the line. Keep it as a warning, or make it a hard stop?

Besides the invoice, we propose keeping four reports: monthly sales per employee, monthly sales per product, quarterly sales per product and the product catalog. We propose dropping the employee email list and the employee phone list, because the employee list page shows the same columns. Please confirm, or name the reports you would swap in. Answer (2026-10-16, demo client): confirmed: the invoice plus monthly sales per employee, monthly sales per product, quarterly sales per product and the product catalog; the employee email and phone lists are dropped.

Order dates carry a time of day, but the sales reports compare them with an end date at midnight. Orders placed on the end date after midnight are therefore left out, including, with the default period, the latest orders themselves. Should the end date count the whole day (our recommendation), or must the new reports keep the current results? Answer (2026-10-16, demo client): keep the current results: the end date is compared at midnight, as in the original; a later change order may change it.

The sales reports and the catalog's lifetime sales count every order whatever its status, including orders that are not yet invoiced or shipped. Is that intended, or should some statuses be excluded? Answer (2026-10-16, demo client): intended: every order counts, whatever its status.

The quarterly product report's chart is fed by the monthly figures, not the quarterly ones. Its quarter labels put the quarter before the year, so a sort on the label would mix years. Should the new report chart quarterly figures and sort quarters by year then quarter? Answer (2026-10-16, demo client): keep the figures the original shows, including the chart fed by the monthly figures; sort quarters by year then quarter.

The catalog is titled as a seasonal (fall) catalog and needs a full PDF render to fill its table of contents. Is one catalog with a generated table of contents enough, or do you need several seasonal editions, and must the catalog be stored after it is generated? Answer (2026-10-16, demo client): one catalog with a generated table of contents, generated on demand and not stored.

The catalog shows a placeholder picture for each category, and the code for real category images is switched off. Should the new catalog show the category images stored with the product categories? Answer (2026-10-16, demo client): keep the original placeholder picture per category. Correction (S1 review, from the design): the question's premise was wrong. The catalog's category header shows the image stored with each category, through a visible attachment control bound to the category image column; the switched-off code is a separate loader of image files, not the stored images. Keeping the original therefore means showing each category's stored image; the design's own comment says the template ships placeholder pictures, which is what the client saw.

A saved query totals each salesperson's sales for the current calendar year, without discounts, but nothing in the application uses it. May we drop it, or is a year-to-date figure per salesperson needed elsewhere, for example on a dashboard? Answer (2026-10-16, demo client): drop the query; no year-to-date figure per salesperson is needed.
